submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 gives the highest efficiency at the 8 kHz allocation. It reaches 92.1% at 35 GeV, against 85.4% for L2 and about 74% for L3. The gap to L2 is about 6.8%, which is larger than the roughly 2% emulation noise. The 40 GeV point is noisy: the first run gave 93.5%, the rerun gave 89.7%, and the mean is 91.6%. That is no better than 35 GeV, so I chose 35 GeV, which is consistent with the prior study. Efficiencies fall off above about 40 GeV. All three candidates are deployable in L1 hardware, and 35 GeV is inside the 20–60 GeV range. One gap in the record: the results never show the measured trigger rate at each threshold. I could not confirm directly that 35 GeV meets the 8 kHz allocation.

requirements.requirement: Highest signal efficiency at allocated rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: L1 at 35 GeV has 92.1% efficiency, the best of the three candidates. L2 is 85.4% and L3 is about 74%. The rate at each threshold was not recorded, so the 8 kHz match is assumed, not confirmed.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm is one of the three candidates
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 was chosen from the three candidates.
L1_deployable = 1, and the other two candidates are also deployable.
